Toyota's first step toward a true software-defined vehicle is starting to reach customers, with our Arene software platform playing a real part in making it possible.
Based on Toyota's internal testing, two numbers from the new RAV4 stand out:
✅ Cockpit voice recognition accuracy climbed from ~70% to 92% compared with a previous system, supported by Arene-based software refinements.
✅ For the latest Toyota Safety Sense system, ~70% of real-world testing was able to be replaced by simulation, with Arene-powered tools taking on more validation work.
Neither result belongs to Arene alone. They came from Toyota teams across hardware, software and testing working together. But they’re an early look at what's possible when software is treated as a core part of vehicle development.
➡️ Learn more about Arene: https://lnkd.in/gnx2WXXx

It’s a wrap for nine interns at our Tokyo office! 👏
This week, our Japan interns completed their time with us. As their final project, they presented their work in a “Genchi Genbutsu” format — an interactive, open-style showcase where they shared the ideas they’d been developing in an informal, discussion-based setting.
From AI models that help make our automated driving systems safer to developing code that accelerates software development and empowers collaboration, our interns made real contributions to shaping the future of mobility.
We can’t wait to see what they do next!

August 25
How do we move from L2+ ADAS toward full autonomy through data-driven development?
At the 2026 American Automotive Summit in Detroit, kensuke yokoi, our Global Head of World Understanding, will explore the real-world journey from rule-based systems to machine learning models in a fireside chat.
Making this transformation requires focusing on three critical areas:
1️⃣ Data foundations & infrastructure: establishing large-scale, diverse data pipelines, continuous iteration loops and the quantitative metrics required for development.
2️⃣ New validation methods: building confidence in machine learning systems whose behavior cannot be fully specified through traditional, requirement-based approaches.
3️⃣ Ecosystem alignment: structuring engineering teams, evaluation frameworks and OEM partnerships to execute the transformation at scale.
Join us September 15, 1:45 PM EST to hear more about the data, evaluation, and partnerships needed to accelerate the path to full autonomy.

My mom still asks me what I actually do for work.
For years I didn't have a good answer. Computers are not her world. Recently I found one that fits: I try to make sure your vehicle still works the way you expect after a software update.
That sounds simple. It isn't, and the reason why says a lot about where the auto industry is right now.
I wrote about it here: https://lnkd.in/g8XwrRFV
-----------
Ma mère me demande périodiquement ce que je fais comme travail, précisément.
Durant plusieurs années, j'ai eu du mal à lui répondre. Comme bien des gens, son monde ne tourne pas autour des ordinateurs et de la technologie. Cependant, récemment je crois avoir une réponse qui soit compréhensible pour elle: Je fais de mon mieux pour faire en sorte que ta voiture fonctionne à chaque fois que tu l'utilises, telle que tu attends et ce, même si son logiciel a été mis à jour dans l'intérim.
Cette mission peut sembler simple, ça ne l'est pas et les raisons pourquoi ce fait existe est révélateur de l'état de l'industrie automobile aujourd'hui. J'ai écrit sur ce sujet récemment: https://lnkd.in/g8XwrRFV

AIM Media House
July 23
Suigen Koide, Head of DevBoost (Generative AI & MLOps), ADAS at Woven by Toyota will be honored with The Vision Award at CDO Vision Tokyo 2026, taking place on 7th August.
The Vision Award honors Chief Data Officers, Chief Analytics Officers, and senior enterprise AI and data leaders driving large-scale data and AI transformation within their organisations.
Suigen is a seasoned technology leader specialising in MLOps and Generative AI at Woven by Toyota, where he drives innovation in machine learning for automated driving systems. Having joined as employee number four on the ADAS ML team, he has spent over eight years building Toyota's machine learning environment for automated driving from the ground up. He is recognised for pioneering MISRA Copilot, a multi-agent system that automates 80 per cent of automotive coding compliance tasks, saving over $1 million and thousands of engineering hours, with the potential to scale to $100 million or more in savings across mission-critical vehicle software. His innovative work on an AI agent for patent generation reduced drafting time from one month to ten minutes, resulting in 70 patent submissions within a single month. He also co-founded SafeML.
Be part of CDO Vision Tokyo, a space to connect with Suigen and industry leaders defining what's next in AI, data, and digital transformation.
